name: Lemeting
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Clynes, Adrian. 2005. Belait. In Adelaar & Himmelmann (eds.), The Austronesian Languages of Asia and Madagascar. Routledge.

new_statements.quote: Lexical roots are typically disyllabic though monosyllabic and trisyllabic roots also exist: tak 'snap (intr), be cut off (of phone)', namumbot 'wasp', kababik 'butterfly'. No examples of quadrisyllabic roots have been noted. Since Belait words often consist of a root and at least one monosyllabic affix, derived lexemes of three syllables frequently occur. See also §2.3 on the preferred size of derived lexemes. Stress is predictably on the final syllable. At the syllable level, there are different possibilities of segment occurrence according to whether a syllable is final or non-final.
new_statements.citation: Clynes, Adrian. 2005. Belait. In K. Alexander Adelaar & Nikolaus P. Himmelmann (eds), The Austronesian Languages of Asia and Madagascar, ch. 15, pp. 429-455. London & New York: Routledge.
new_statements.locator: §2.2 Morpheme and syllable structure, p. 432 (between the running headers '432 THE AUSTRONESIAN LANGUAGES' and 'BELAIT 433' in the scanned stream; §2 Phonology = pp. 430-433 per the book's table of contents)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the last syllable of the word (roots are mostly disyllabic; affixed lexemes of three syllables are common and still take final stress).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the recovered text.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated in the recovered text; §2.3 (preferred size of derived lexemes) and the clitic discussion (§3.7 mentions one proclitic an=) were not recovered and might qualify the rule for affixed/cliticised forms.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexical roots and derived lexemes) as described for the Metting dialect (the chapter's basis); Clynes states all dialects share the segment inventory but says nothing dialect-specific about stress. The sentence is verbatim scanned from the Internet Archive scan, obtained through Open Library search-inside snippets, not from a page image; scanned of this sentence is clean.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog bela1260 'Lemeting' = Belait [beg]; Clynes 2005 describes the Metting (Meting) dialect of Kampong Mungkom, Kiudang (Tutong district), with comparative notes on the Labi and Kuala Balai dialects; 'Belait' historically also labelled other groups (Bisaya, Tabun, etc.), but the language described is Lemeting/Metting as Glottolog intends.
